relevance_note: Case report of one girl with a NOD2 variant and EOS/Blau syndrome: "WES revealed a de novo heterozygous mutation in NOD2".
method_note: Single case report; read in full by hand, JSON assembled with a short Python script in the scratch directory (values typed from reading, not transcribed by script). In scope: the patient (label 'patient', rule 5) and her two parents, who were sequenced and did not carry the variant; their sex is not stated, so they are 'parent of patient' and 'parent of patient 2'. Parents have no variant rows and no features ('lack of family history' is too general to exclude specific features). Age at diagnosis of EOS/Blau not stated; the 'diagnosed at an unusually young age of 6 years' refers to GCTTS, recorded as onset of that feature, not as disease diagnosis age. Polyarticular arthritis onset 'by age 7' is from the abstract. Variant type 'missense' from the sentence naming R334Q among missense mutations of residue 334. In silico predictions (SIFT, Polyphen2, CADD) are not functional assays, so functional_evidence is not reported. Normal labs recorded as excluded abnormalities under D-27; whole normal ophthalmology/dermatology examinations recorded as stated and not used to exclude cataract, glaucoma, erythema nodosum etc. Normal creatinine not used to exclude the composite 'granulomatous nephritis or renal failure'. Arthritis and joint swelling resolved after 1 year of treatment ('no evidence of joint swelling, joint tenderness or restricted range of motion'); treated as a follow-up course, not a contradiction, so arthritis remains observed. 'suggestive of active synovitis' is hedged and not recorded as its own feature. No contradictions found.
